sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 佐兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download The New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, President Trump, conservatives, and the NRA are all again pointing to mental illness in response to a school shooting.
sentences.zh: 今天，特朗普总统、保守派人士和全国步枪协会（NRA）再次在回应校园枪击案时指向了精神疾病。

sentences.en: But how can the mental health system stop a shooting when most shooters aren't mentally ill?
sentences.zh: 但是，当大多数枪手并没有精神疾病时，心理健康系统又该如何阻止枪击事件呢？

sentences.en: It's Friday, February 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月23日，星期五。

sentences.en: I believe that this insane monster should have ever been able to obtain a firearm.
sentences.zh: 我相信这个疯狂的怪物根本就不应该有机会获得枪支。

sentences.en: Ever.
sentences.zh: 绝不应该。

sentences.en: I do not think that he should have gotten his hands on any kind of weapon.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他应该有机会接触到任何种类的武器。

sentences.en: That's number one.
sentences.zh: 这是第一点。

sentences.en: This individual was nuts.
sentences.zh: 这个人是个疯子。

sentences.en: We don't know right now exactly why this deranged individual did this.
sentences.zh: 我们现在还不清楚这个精神错乱的人为什么要这样做。

sentences.en: Crazy madman bent on evil.
sentences.zh: 一个一心作恶的疯狂恶棍。

sentences.en: And a wacko came in and shot the five of them.
sentences.zh: 一个怪胎闯进来，射杀了他们五个人。

sentences.en: Who were shot by this madman.
sentences.zh: 他们被这个疯子射杀了。

sentences.en: They're homicidal maniacs.
sentences.zh: 他们是杀人狂魔。

sentences.en: People like this with mental health issues.
sentences.zh: 像这样有心理健康问题的人。

sentences.en: This troubled young man fell through the cracks.
sentences.zh: 这个陷入困境的年轻人被社会遗忘了。

sentences.en: The failure of America's mental health system.
sentences.zh: 美国心理健康系统的失败。

sentences.en: This is a mental health problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个心理健康问题。

sentences.en: There is a mental health epidemic here which is being confused for a gun problem.
sentences.zh: 这里存在一种心理健康流行病，却被误认为是枪支问题。

sentences.en: Again, this is a mental health issue.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这是一个心理健康问题。

sentences.en: This is not a gun issue.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是枪支问题。

sentences.en: The common theme with these kinds of shootings is mental illness.
sentences.zh: 这类枪击事件的共同点就是精神疾病。

sentences.en: And this is something that we should not be ignoring.
sentences.zh: 这是我们不应该忽视的问题。

sentences.en: Would you like me to...
sentences.zh: 你想让我……

sentences.en: How would you like me to refer to you?
sentences.zh: 你想让我怎么称呼你？

sentences.en: Doctor?
sentences.zh: 医生？

sentences.en: Professionally, Dr. BarnhorSt.
sentences.zh: 在职业场合，叫我巴恩霍斯特医生。

sentences.en: Personally, you can always call me Amy.
sentences.zh: 私下里，你随时可以叫我艾米。

sentences.en: But professionally, Dr. BarnhorSt.
sentences.zh: 但在职业场合，请叫我巴恩霍斯特医生。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, Dr. Barnhorst, tell me about the day of this appointment.
sentences.zh: 那么，巴恩霍斯特医生，跟我说说这次预约那天的情况吧。

sentences.en: Well, it started out as just a usual day in a busy crisis unit.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那只是繁忙危机处理中心里平常的一天。

sentences.en: So, I work as an emergency psychiatrist in a crisis unit that's adjacent to an inpatient psychiatric hospital in California.
sentences.zh: 我在加州一家紧邻住院精神病院的危机处理中心担任急诊精神科医生。

sentences.en: We see people who are acutely ill or acutely in crisis.
sentences.zh: 我们接待的是病情急性发作或处于急性危机中的人。

sentences.en: Maybe people feeling suicidal and depressed.
sentences.zh: 也许是感到自杀倾向和抑郁的人。

sentences.en: Maybe some folks who were brought in because they were hearing voices.
sentences.zh: 也许是一些因为听到幻听而被送来的人。

sentences.en: And then the police brought this kid in.
sentences.zh: 然后警察把这个孩子带了过来。

sentences.en: He was a 21-year-old.
sentences.zh: 他21岁。

sentences.en: And his parents had called the cops because they had gotten concerned about some of the stuff he'd been posting on social media.
sentences.zh: 他的父母报了警，因为他们对他发布在社交媒体上的一些内容感到担忧。

sentences.en: His posts had kind of gotten increasingly hostile but were generally vague up until, you know,
sentences.zh: 他的帖子变得越来越具有敌意，但总体上比较模糊，直到，你知道，

sentences.en: the last few days where he had made some specific references to the Columbine shooting.
sentences.zh: 最后几天，他提到了一些关于科伦拜恩枪击案的具体内容。

sentences.en: And something about some death and destruction.
sentences.zh: 还有一些关于死亡和破坏的内容。

sentences.en: And one of the things he referred to in his Facebook page was a day of retribution.
sentences.zh: 他在Facebook页面上提到的其中一件事是“报复日”。

sentences.en: And when the police went to his house and spoke with the parents, the brother mentioned that this patient had told him he was going to try to buy a gun.
sentences.zh: 当警察去他家与父母交谈时，他的兄弟提到这个病人曾告诉他，他打算去买一把枪。

sentences.en: And the brother thought he had done so but wasn't sure.
sentences.zh: 他兄弟以为他已经买了，但不确定。

sentences.en: And why did the police bring him to your office?
sentences.zh: 为什么警察把他带到你的办公室？

sentences.en: They've been told about this posting on Facebook, which is alarming.
sentences.zh: 他们被告知了Facebook上的这个帖子，这很令人担忧。

sentences.en: Why did they bring him to you?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们把他带给你？

sentences.en: Well, he really hadn't committed a crime.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他实际上并没有犯罪。

sentences.en: So they couldn't arrest him.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不能逮捕他。

sentences.en: But I imagine that the police were pretty worried about this guy.
sentences.zh: 但我猜警察对这个人非常担心。

sentences.en: You know, he certainly had a lot of concerning signs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他确实有很多令人担忧的迹象。

sentences.en: And I think they brought him to us in the hopes that maybe the mental health system would be a way that we could prevent him from going down a bad path.
sentences.zh: 我想他们把他带给我们，是希望心理健康系统能成为阻止他走上歧途的一种方式。

sentences.en: So what are you doing first?
sentences.zh: 那么你首先要做什么？

sentences.en: What's your role in this moment?
sentences.zh: 此刻你的角色是什么？

sentences.en: So my first thing is I get the chart and I flip through it and kind of see what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我首先要做的是拿到病历，翻阅一下，看看发生了什么。

sentences.en: For this young man, I probably would have had any records we had on him, which was none.
sentences.zh: 对于这个年轻人，我可能没有任何关于他的记录，实际上确实没有。

sentences.en: And the legal hold that the police brought him in on, which was just a piece of paper with a few lines, might be something as simple as making threatening postings on Facebook,
sentences.zh: 警察带他来时所依据的法律拘留令，只是一张写着几行字的纸，内容可能很简单，比如在Facebook上发布威胁性帖子，

sentences.en: comma, might have bought guns, says brother, comma, parents worried.
sentences.zh: 逗号，可能买了枪，据其兄弟所说，逗号，父母很担心。

sentences.en: In this case, I had fairly little except that ominous information.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，除了那些不祥的信息外，我几乎一无所知。

sentences.en: So I always build a picture in my mind of what people are going to be like before I meet them.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是在见到人之前，先在脑海中构建一个关于他们会是什么样子的形象。

sentences.en: But he did not really jive with my mental image that I had built up.
sentences.zh: 但他与我脑海中构建的形象并不太吻合。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: If I had met this young man and he seemed, for example, like in a manic episode where he was impulsive, where he was talking really fast, where he was delusional and grandiose,
sentences.zh: 如果我见到这个年轻人，他看起来，比如，处于躁狂发作期，表现得冲动、说话很快、有妄想和夸大倾向，

sentences.en: that might be indicative that he was, in fact, mentally ill.
sentences.zh: 那可能表明他确实患有精神疾病。

sentences.en: And that maybe this idea about threatening up his school was secondary to a mental illness that could be treated and thereby we could prevent the shooting or the act of violence.
sentences.zh: 也许他威胁学校的想法是继发于某种可以治疗的精神疾病，从而我们可以预防枪击或暴力行为。

sentences.en: But in the case of him, I mean, he looked not like somebody with a mental illness.
sentences.zh: 但在他这个案例中，我的意思是，他看起来不像是一个患有精神疾病的人。

sentences.en: He didn't have any of those signs.
sentences.zh: 他没有任何那些迹象。

sentences.en: He was a nice enough kid, not particularly angry to me, although it was easy to see that he had some darkness in him.
sentences.zh: 他是个挺不错的孩子，对我来说并没有特别愤怒，尽管很容易看出他内心有一些阴暗面。

sentences.en: And I think he was a little sullen and depressed, not happy with his social standing and how things had been going at his school.
sentences.zh: 我想他有点郁郁寡欢，对自己的社会地位以及在学校里的处境感到不满。

sentences.en: He said that he didn't think he had a mental illness.
sentences.zh: 他说他不认为自己有精神疾病。

sentences.en: He didn't want treatment.
sentences.zh: 他不想接受治疗。

sentences.en: He didn't need treatment.
sentences.zh: 他不需要治疗。

sentences.en: I feel like a sad, brooding kid who was hurt and realized he had done something wrong and really wanted to go home.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他是一个悲伤、忧郁的孩子，他受了伤，意识到自己做错了事，真的很想回家。

sentences.en: So ultimately, you're trying to determine if this post on Facebook was coming from a place of mental illness or possibly something else.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，你是在试图确定Facebook上的这个帖子是源于精神疾病，还是其他原因。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I'm trying to figure out if he is going to meet criteria to be involuntarily admitted to a psychiatric hospital.
sentences.zh: 所以我正在试图弄清楚他是否符合被强制送入精神病院的标准。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And in California, in order to be admitted to a psychiatric hospital involuntarily, you have to meet one of three criteria to either be dangerous to yourself,
sentences.zh: 在加州，要被强制送入精神病院，你必须符合以下三个标准之一：对自己构成危险，

sentences.en: dangerous to somebody else, or gravely disabled, which means that you're not able to provide for your own basic needs like your food, clothing, and shelter.
sentences.zh: 对他人构成危险，或者严重残疾，这意味着你无法满足自己的基本需求，如食物、衣物和住所。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So even if this young man is angry or showing a propensity towards violence,
sentences.zh: 所以即使这个年轻人很愤怒或表现出暴力倾向，

sentences.en: you need to determine that these emotions are coming from a mental illness in order to involuntarily commit him.
sentences.zh: 你也需要确定这些情绪是源于精神疾病，才能对他进行强制收治。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So at this point, I'm making a primarily clinical decision about whether or not I should meet this young man for treatment.
sentences.zh: 所以此时，我主要是在做一个临床决定，关于我是否应该收治这个年轻人进行治疗。

sentences.en: But I also know that my clinical decisions have legal implications for him because there is a difference between an admission to a hospital and a commitment.
sentences.zh: 但我也知道我的临床决定对他有法律影响，因为住院和强制收治之间是有区别的。

sentences.en: As a commitment, as a doctor, what I do is I make the clinical decision to admit someone to a hospital.
sentences.zh: 作为强制收治，作为医生，我所做的是做出收治某人住院的临床决定。

sentences.en: The commitment is a legal process that is done by the judge or the hearing officer.
sentences.zh: 强制收治是由法官或听证官执行的法律程序。

sentences.en: And that's the checks and balances in the system that make sure that some doctor can't just admit people willy-nilly and hold them in a hospital indefinitely with no liberties.
sentences.zh: 这是系统中的制衡机制，确保医生不能随意收治他人，并将他们无限期地关在医院里，剥夺他们的自由。

sentences.en: And so if he is committed, then his name goes into a federal database of people who are prohibited from purchasing guns.
sentences.zh: 如果他被强制收治，他的名字就会进入一个联邦数据库，记录那些被禁止购买枪支的人。

sentences.en: And any time a federally licensed dealer does a background check, his name will come up as a prohibited person, and he won't be able to buy a gun.
sentences.zh: 任何时候，联邦许可的经销商进行背景调查时，他的名字都会显示为被禁止人员，他就无法购买枪支。

sentences.en: But he'll still be able to purchase from private party sales and from internet sales and from gun shows, where in most states they don't do background checks.
sentences.zh: 但他仍然可以通过私人交易、互联网销售和枪支展销会购买，在大多数州，这些渠道不进行背景调查。

sentences.en: And so this is how someone like you interacts with what most people think of as the federal background check system that's used for gun purchases.
sentences.zh: 这就是像你这样的人如何与大多数人认为的用于购枪的联邦背景调查系统进行互动的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Doctor, this feels very complicated, what you're describing, because so often people are expressing violent thoughts, but mental illness is not clear.
sentences.zh: 医生，你描述的情况感觉非常复杂，因为人们经常表达暴力想法，但精神疾病并不明确。

sentences.en: And yet, as a doctor, you want to prevent them from carrying out these acts, I assume.
sentences.zh: 然而，作为医生，我想你一定希望阻止他们实施这些行为。

sentences.en: So how do you grapple with people who fall short of that glaring mental illness, but who are expressing violent thoughts?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是如何处理那些没有达到明显精神疾病标准，但却表达了暴力想法的人的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard, because we do see people every day, especially in a crisis setting, that we want to help, but they don't meet the criteria for involuntary help.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很难，因为我们每天都会见到一些人，特别是在危机处理环境中，我们想帮助他们，但他们不符合强制帮助的标准。

sentences.en: And they don't want help.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也不想要帮助。

sentences.en: And so we have to let them go.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不得不让他们离开。

sentences.en: And sometimes that involves people with the potential for violence.
sentences.zh: 有时这涉及到有暴力潜力的人。

sentences.en: And it is a balance between people's civil liberties and their right to make choices that I may not think are the best choices.
sentences.zh: 这是人们的公民自由与他们做出我认为并非最佳选择的权利之间的一种平衡。

sentences.en: It's really hard, from the vantage point of being a psychiatrist, to prevent violence, since most violence is not caused by mental illness.
sentences.zh: 从精神科医生的角度来看，预防暴力确实很难，因为大多数暴力并非由精神疾病引起。

sentences.en: About 4% of community violence is attributable to severe mental illness.
sentences.zh: 社区暴力中约有4%可归因于严重精神疾病。

sentences.en: So that would mean that 96% of the rest of violence that occurs in a community has nothing to do with mental illness.
sentences.zh: 那意味着社区中发生的其余96%的暴力事件与精神疾病毫无关系。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: Do you know how mental illness relates to mass shootings, specifically, in terms of cause and effect and scale?
sentences.zh: 你知道精神疾病与大规模枪击事件在因果关系和规模上具体是如何关联的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, so this is a tricky question we get into semantics a little bit here, because, you know, it's hard to stand by an argument that people who make posts like this,
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这是一个棘手的问题，我们在这里有点纠结于语义，因为，你知道，很难坚持认为那些发布这种帖子的人，

sentences.en: or that anybody who goes into a school and opens fire on students, is some paragon of psychological well-being.
sentences.zh: 或者任何走进学校向学生开火的人，是心理健康的典范。

sentences.en: I mean, I think everybody would agree that these people are not mentally well, per se.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想每个人都会同意这些人本身并不精神健康。

sentences.en: But that is really different than actually having a specific mental illness, like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder or major depressive disorder.
sentences.zh: 但这与真正患有特定的精神疾病，如精神分裂症、双相情感障碍或重度抑郁症，是有很大区别的。

sentences.en: A lot of the characters of these mass shooters are similar.
sentences.zh: 这些大规模枪手的许多特征是相似的。

sentences.en: And that's not to say that none of them have mental illness, because some have.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说他们中没有人患有精神疾病，因为有些人确实有。

sentences.en: But a lot of them are just really angry, resentful, bitter young men who have similar histories of social isolation, they've been bullied, they've harbored revenge fantasies,
sentences.zh: 但他们中的许多人只是非常愤怒、怨恨、痛苦的年轻人，他们有相似的社会孤立史，曾被欺凌，怀有复仇幻想，

sentences.en: they have an entitlement towards social standing, towards attention for women.
sentences.zh: 他们对社会地位、对女性的关注有一种权利感。

sentences.en: They feel like they're not getting the popularity, the attention, the recognition.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得没有得到应有的欢迎、关注和认可。

sentences.en: That they deserve.
sentences.zh: 他们应得的。

sentences.en: That they deserve.
sentences.zh: 他们应得的。

sentences.en: So there's this idea that they're better than everybody thinks they are, and they kind of want to show the world that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有一种想法，认为自己比别人认为的要好，他们想向世界展示这一点。

sentences.en: So how would the treatment of someone like that differ from the kind of treatment they would need if they were determined to be mentally ill?
sentences.zh: 那么，对这样的人的治疗，与如果他们被确定为患有精神疾病时所需的治疗有何不同？

sentences.en: It seems like in either case, some kind of treatment is needed.
sentences.zh: 似乎无论哪种情况，都需要某种治疗。

sentences.en: So what's the difference?
sentences.zh: 那么区别是什么？

sentences.en: Well, one of the big differences, you know, we do have medications for things like schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最大的区别之一是，你知道，我们确实有治疗精神分裂症和双相情感障碍等疾病的药物。

sentences.en: We don't have medications for things like resentment, hatred, anger at the world.
sentences.zh: 我们没有治疗怨恨、仇恨、对世界愤怒等问题的药物。

sentences.en: We can't fix that so well.
sentences.zh: 我们无法很好地解决这些问题。

sentences.en: So there's no way to like admit somebody like that to a psychiatric hospital, treat them over the course of the two weeks that we might be able to have them,
sentences.zh: 所以没有办法把这样的人送进精神病院，在我们可能拥有的两周时间里治疗他们，

sentences.en: and then completely change the personality that they've spent their whole life building up.
sentences.zh: 然后彻底改变他们一生建立起来的人格。

sentences.en: And it sounds like this young man who's standing in front of you fits that profile more than one of a clearly mentally ill person.
sentences.zh: 听起来站在你面前的这个年轻人比一个明显的精神病患者更符合这种特征。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: He fits the profile of the angry, socially isolated young man with no mental health history.
sentences.zh: 他符合那个愤怒、社会孤立、没有心理健康病史的年轻人的特征。

sentences.en: So what's going through your head as you make this decision whether or not to admit him?
sentences.zh: 那么，当你决定是否收治他时，你在想什么？

sentences.en: So in my mind, I'm thinking to myself, this young man does not appear to be mentally ill to me.
sentences.zh: 在我的脑海里，我在想，这个年轻人看起来并不像患有精神疾病。

sentences.en: He does appear to potentially be dangerous, but that's not something that is going to be changed by admitting him to a psychiatric hospital.
sentences.zh: 他看起来确实有可能具有危险性，但这并不是通过把他送进精神病院就能改变的。

sentences.en: And if I send him home, then I'm concerned that I, you know, had my chance to intervene with the next mass shooter and I did nothing.
sentences.zh: 如果我让他回家，那么我担心我，你知道，错过了干预下一个大规模枪手的机会，而我什么也没做。

sentences.en: And now he's back home with his gun.
sentences.zh: 现在他带着枪回家了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 即便是在黑胶唱片盛行的年代，我还在夜店当DJ的时候，你每晚都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个活生生的、充满50年历史精美文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜欢的播客平台上收听奥德马斯·皮格特出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能让你免费试用一个月，且无需绑定信用卡，去探索《纽约时报》呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序，即可免费使用第一个月。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看时报订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载时报应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Dr. Barnhorst, you've spoken to this young man.
sentences.zh: 那么，巴恩霍斯特医生，你已经和这位年轻人谈过了。

sentences.en: You've learned that he has posted on Facebook something quite scary.
sentences.zh: 你了解到他在Facebook上发布了一些相当可怕的内容。

sentences.en: You've learned that he may have just purchased a gun you don't know.
sentences.zh: 你了解到他可能刚买了一把枪，而你对此一无所知。

sentences.en: And now it's your job to decide whether or not to commit him for a serious mental illness.
sentences.zh: 现在你的工作是决定是否要以严重的精神疾病为由将他强制收治。

sentences.en: What do you decide to do?
sentences.zh: 你决定怎么做？

sentences.en: He did not look to me like he had a mental illness.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，他并不像患有精神疾病。

sentences.en: He did not look to me like he technically met the standards for our involuntary commitment.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，他从技术上讲并不符合我们强制收治的标准。

sentences.en: But I really didn't want to be wrong.
sentences.zh: 但我真的不想判断失误。

sentences.en: And in the end, I decided to admit him because there's some leeway in the statute.
sentences.zh: 最终，我决定收治他，因为法律条文中留有一些余地。

sentences.en: So it's ultimately up to the judge to make the decision of whether or not he gets committed officially.
sentences.zh: 所以，最终是否正式收治他，取决于法官的决定。

sentences.en: So I admitted him.
sentences.zh: 所以我收治了他。

sentences.en: So you erred on the side of caution to get him into this kind of mental health legal pipeline.
sentences.zh: 所以你是为了谨慎起见，把他纳入了这种心理健康法律程序中。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It sounds, Dr., like you're saying part of you understood quite clearly that he might not be mentally ill.
sentences.zh: 医生，听起来你似乎在说，你内心很清楚他可能并没有精神疾病。

sentences.en: But you were making a kind of civic as well as medical decision to keep him out of the general population.
sentences.zh: 但你是在做一种公民层面以及医疗层面的决定，目的是让他远离普通人群。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the principles of practicing medicine is that the higher the risk of the possibility, the more certain you want to be that it's not the case.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，行医的原则之一是：风险的可能性越高，你就越希望确保这种风险不会发生。

sentences.en: So if I'm worried that somebody might or might not go home and punch a wall, I'm willing to be fairly liberal in making a mistake there.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我担心某人可能会或不会回家去打墙，我愿意在犯错这件事上相当宽容。

sentences.en: Much more so liberal than if I'm worried somebody might or might not go home and shoot up a school.
sentences.zh: 这比我担心某人可能会或不会回家去学校开枪要宽容得多。

sentences.en: You can live with one, not the other.
sentences.zh: 前者你可以接受，后者则不行。

sentences.en: I am willing to let them a little bit of freedom.
sentences.zh: 我愿意给他们一点点自由。

sentences.en: If the risk of my giving them some freedom and letting them go is that they might shoot a bunch of people into school, I need to be really,
sentences.zh: 如果我给他们一些自由并放他们走，而风险是他们可能会在学校射杀一群人，那我必须非常、

sentences.en: really confident that I'm right and that that is not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 非常确信我是对的，而且那种事不会发生。

sentences.en: And what happened?
sentences.zh: 后来发生了什么？

sentences.en: I admitted him to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 我把他收治进了医院。

sentences.en: He went before the hearing officer a few days later, and the hearing officer determined that he was not dangerous because of a mental illness.
sentences.zh: 几天后他出席了听证会，听证官认定他并没有因精神疾病而构成危险。

sentences.en: And then he's no longer involuntarily held, so he's free to go.
sentences.zh: 于是他不再被强制拘留，可以自由离开了。

sentences.en: So you had to let him go.
sentences.zh: 所以你不得不放他走。

sentences.en: The system had to let him go.
sentences.zh: 体制不得不放他走。

sentences.en: Yeah, we had to let him go.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们不得不放他走。

sentences.en: So, doctor, does this man end up on the federal background check system, given the way this is played out?
sentences.zh: 那么，医生，考虑到事态的发展，这个人最终会被录入联邦背景调查系统吗？

sentences.en: No, because the judge did not certify his commitment in court.
sentences.zh: 不会，因为法官没有在法庭上证明他的收治必要性。

sentences.en: He does not land on the federal background check system's list of prohibited persons.
sentences.zh: 他不会出现在联邦背景调查系统的禁止持枪人员名单上。

sentences.en: But because I admitted him to the hospital, he does meet criteria for a five-year prohibition just within California.
sentences.zh: 但因为我把他收治进了医院，他确实符合加州境内五年的禁枪标准。

sentences.en: That prohibition will expire in a couple years.
sentences.zh: 这项禁令将在几年后到期。

sentences.en: And were he to move to another state, he would still be able to buy a firearm there in the meantime.
sentences.zh: 如果他搬到另一个州，在此期间他仍然可以买到枪。

sentences.en: Do you think that this system failed this young man in this moment and, as a result, failed the rest of us?
sentences.zh: 你认为这个系统在这一刻辜负了这个年轻人，并因此辜负了我们其他人吗？

sentences.en: You know, it's hard for me to say that this system failed this young man because this young man is not who the system was set up to help.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我很难说这个系统辜负了这个年轻人，因为这个年轻人并不是该系统旨在帮助的对象。

sentences.en: He's not somebody that we have a treatment or a cure for because he wasn't mentally ill.
sentences.zh: 他不是我们有治疗方法或治愈手段的人，因为他没有精神疾病。

sentences.en: The unfortunate part is the criminal system couldn't help him either because he hadn't done anything criminal.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，刑事司法系统也帮不了他，因为他没有做任何犯罪行为。

sentences.en: So what do you think when you hear gun rights advocates talking now so much about mental health?
sentences.zh: 那么，当你听到枪支权利倡导者现在如此频繁地谈论心理健康时，你是怎么想的？

sentences.en: Do you think there's an understanding of what that actually means in practice?
sentences.zh: 你认为他们理解这在实践中到底意味着什么吗？

sentences.en: I think there's not.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们不理解。

sentences.en: And I think it's important for folks to have a better sense of what it looks like played out in practice, which is it doesn't look very good.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，让人们更好地了解它在实践中是如何运作的很重要，而实际情况并不乐观。

sentences.en: There's not a lot that in actuality we can do for these people.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们能为这些人做的事情并不多。

sentences.en: And the irony is,
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，

sentences.en: I think a lot of the folks who point towards the mental health system as being a less restrictive way of decreasing gun violence because they don't want to lose their rights to own firearMs.
sentences.zh: 我认为很多将心理健康系统视为减少枪支暴力的一种限制较少的方法的人，是因为他们不想失去拥有枪支的权利。

sentences.en: The part of that they're missing because they don't see what happens in the real mental health world is that if we were going to really try to prevent violence and mass shootings within the mental health system,
sentences.zh: 他们忽略的部分是——因为他们看不到真实的心理健康世界里发生了什么——如果我们真的想尝试在心理健康系统内预防暴力和大规模枪击事件，

sentences.en: we would have to expand the net of who we were allowed to involuntarily detain and hold enormously in order to find those one or two people in thousands that might actually perpetrate mass violence.
sentences.zh: 我们就必须极大地扩大我们被允许强制拘留和收治的人群范围，才能在成千上万的人中找到那一个或两个可能真正实施大规模暴力的人。

sentences.en: Would we have to therefore expand the definition of mental illness?
sentences.zh: 那么我们是否必须因此扩大精神疾病的定义？

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard to expand the definition of an illness,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很难扩大一种疾病的定义，

sentences.en: but I think we would be talking about dramatically expanding the reaches of the mental health system and largely the involuntary mental health system because mostly we're looking for people who are not seeking treatment on their own.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们谈论的是大幅扩大心理健康系统的覆盖范围，主要是强制性的心理健康系统，因为我们寻找的主要是那些不主动寻求治疗的人。

sentences.en: So what that looks like is that we would lower the bar really far in terms of who we would be able to involuntarily commit.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着，我们将大幅降低强制收治的门槛。

sentences.en: And it would be almost every angry young man who had a history of social isolation, being bullied, who had an interest in violent video games and collecting guns,
sentences.zh: 那几乎会涵盖每一个有社交孤立史、被霸凌过、对暴力电子游戏和收集枪支感兴趣的愤怒年轻人，

sentences.en: whoever made macabre-sounding Facebook posts or comments about wishing everybody at his school were dead.
sentences.zh: 以及任何在Facebook上发表过令人毛骨悚然的言论，或评论说希望学校里所有人都死掉的人。

sentences.en: That's actually a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 那实际上是很多人。

sentences.en: And it's easy in hindsight to look at mass shooters and say they showed all the warning signs.
sentences.zh: 事后诸葛亮地去看大规模枪击案的凶手，说他们表现出了所有的预警信号，这很容易。

sentences.en: But when you look forward,
sentences.zh: 但当你向前看时，

sentences.en: that's a lot of people that you would have to take out of their world and out of their lives and involuntarily detained in the mental health system and probably to not much end.
sentences.zh: 你必须把那么多人从他们的世界和生活中带走，强制关进心理健康系统，而且很可能没什么结果。

sentences.en: What do you mean to not much end?
sentences.zh: 你说的“没什么结果”是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, eventually we have to let them go.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最终我们还是得放他们走。

sentences.en: It's unlikely that we'd be able to fix them.
sentences.zh: 我们不太可能治好他们。

sentences.en: So even if we were allowed to keep them for three weeks or three months, I don't know that we would be really solving the problem.
sentences.zh: 所以即使我们被允许把他们关三周或三个月，我也不知道我们是否真的解决了问题。

sentences.en: We would just be keeping them out of circulation for a little while.
sentences.zh: 我们只是让他们暂时脱离了社会。

sentences.en: Doctor, I wonder how often you think about this young man who you admitted and then who the court system let go and who now roams the world.
sentences.zh: 医生，我很好奇你多久会想起这个被你收治、后来被法院系统释放、现在游荡在世界上的年轻人。

sentences.en: I think about him every time there's a school shooting.
sentences.zh: 每次发生校园枪击案时，我都会想起他。

sentences.en: Doctor, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 医生，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的消息。

sentences.en: Please welcome the executive vice president of the National Rifle Association, Wayne LaPierre.
sentences.zh: 请欢迎全国步枪协会执行副主席韦恩·拉皮埃尔。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I appreciate this opportunity.
sentences.zh: 我很珍惜这个机会。

sentences.en: We have serious discussions ahead and serious issues that impact each and every one of us.
sentences.zh: 我们面前有严肃的讨论，也有影响我们每一个人的严肃议题。

sentences.en: On Thursday, after a week of silence since the school shooting in Florida, the head of the NRA spoke out at an annual gathering of conservative activists.
sentences.zh: 周四，在佛罗里达州校园枪击案发生一周的沉默后，全国步枪协会（NRA）负责人在一场保守派活动人士的年度集会上发表了讲话。

sentences.en: As usual, the opportunists wasted not one second to exploit tragedy for political gain.
sentences.zh: 像往常一样，机会主义者们一秒钟都没有浪费，利用悲剧来获取政治利益。

sentences.en: They hate the NRA.
sentences.zh: 他们痛恨NRA。

sentences.en: They hate the Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: 他们痛恨宪法第二修正案。

sentences.en: They hate individual freedom.
sentences.zh: 他们痛恨个人自由。

sentences.en: LaPierre rejected growing calls for stricter gun control and instead proposed, as he has in the past, that schools across the U.S.
sentences.zh: 拉皮埃尔拒绝了日益高涨的加强枪支管制的呼声，转而像过去一样提议，美国各地的学校

sentences.en: protect themselves with armed guards.
sentences.zh: 应该用武装警卫来保护自己。

sentences.en: Our jewelry stores all over this country are more important than our children.
sentences.zh: 我们全国各地的珠宝店都比我们的孩子更重要。

sentences.en: Our banks, our airports, our NBA games, our NFL games, our office buildings, our movie stars, our politicians.
sentences.zh: 我们的银行、机场、NBA比赛、NFL比赛、办公楼、电影明星、政客们。

sentences.en: They're all more protected than our children at school.
sentences.zh: 他们都比学校里的孩子受到更好的保护。

sentences.en: Does that make any sense to anybody?
sentences.zh: 这对任何人来说有意义吗？

sentences.en: I want my schools protected just like my banks are protected.
sentences.zh: 我希望我的学校能像我的银行一样受到保护。

sentences.en: At the White House on Thursday, President Trump had a similar message.
sentences.zh: 周四在白宫，特朗普总统传达了类似的信息。

sentences.en: We have to harden our schools, not soften them up.
sentences.zh: 我们必须加强学校的安保，而不是削弱它。

sentences.en: A gun-free zone to a killer or somebody that wants to be a killer.
sentences.zh: 对于杀手或想要成为杀手的人来说，无枪区，

sentences.en: That's like going in for the ice cream.
sentences.zh: 就像是去吃冰淇淋一样。

sentences.en: That's like, here I am, take me.
sentences.zh: 就像是说，我在这儿，来抓我吧。

sentences.en: Trump reiterated a proposal made earlier in the week that teachers be armed.
sentences.zh: 特朗普重申了本周早些时候提出的建议，即武装教师。

sentences.en: This time, he suggested giving bonuses to teachers who are qualified to carry a weapon.
sentences.zh: 这一次，他建议给有资格携带武器的教师发放奖金。

sentences.en: Frankly, they'd feel more comfortable having the gun anyway, but you give them a little bit of a bonus.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，他们本来就觉得带枪更舒服，但你再给他们一点奖金。

sentences.en: So practically for free, you have now made the school into a hardened target.
sentences.zh: 所以几乎是免费的，你现在就把学校变成了一个坚固的目标。

sentences.en: On Thursday afternoon, the Sheriff's Department in Broward County, Florida, announced that the only armed deputy stationed at Stoneman Douglas High School
sentences.zh: 周四下午，佛罗里达州布劳沃德县警长办公室宣布，驻扎在斯通曼·道格拉斯高中的唯一一名武装副警长

sentences.en: had taken cover in the parking lot outside, rather than going into the building when the shooting began.
sentences.zh: 在枪击开始时，躲在了外面的停车场，而不是进入大楼。

sentences.en: The Daily is produced by Theo Balcom, Lindsay Garrison, Rachel Quester, Annie Brown, Andy Mills,
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》由西奥·巴尔科姆、琳赛·加里森、雷切尔·奎斯特、安妮·布朗、安迪·米尔斯制作，

sentences.en: Ike Srees-Kandaraja, Claire Tennesketter, Paige Cowett, and Michael Simon-Johnson, with editing help from Larissa Anderson.
sentences.zh: 艾克·斯里斯-坎达拉贾、克莱尔·坦内斯凯特、佩奇·考特和迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊参与制作，拉里萨·安德森提供编辑帮助。

sentences.en: Lisa Tobin is our executive producer.
sentences.zh: 丽莎·托宾是我们的执行制片人。

sentences.en: Samantha Hennig is our editorial director.
sentences.zh: 萨曼莎·亨尼格是我们的编辑总监。

sentences.en: Our technical manager is Brad Fisher.
sentences.zh: 我们的技术经理是布拉德·费舍尔。

sentences.en: And our sound engineer is Peter Sale.
sentences.zh: 我们的音响工程师是彼得·塞尔。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Sam Dolmick, Michaela Bouchard, and Aura de Kornfeld.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢萨姆·多尔米克、米凯拉·布沙尔和奥拉·德·科恩菲尔德。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是一个非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何地方收听《Wirecutter秀》。
